title: Butterfly wing patterns in flight create powerful illusory motion cues.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the whole GitHub repository tree and opened Analysis_02_Collins/DF_EMD.csv (4,740 rows = 790 wing morphotypes x 6 render treatments, 413 species names; columns are EMD (elementary motion detector, a computer model of motion vision) energy means and SDs in four directions), DF_Pattern_Analysis.csv (1,580 rows = 790 morphotypes x 2 wings, 29 pattern-statistic columns), DF_Info_Table.csv (399 species with family/subfamily/tribe), Analysis_01_Takeoff/EMD_Output.csv (9,564 per-frame EMD rows from 16 filmed butterflies) and one behavioural file, Results_P001.csv (45 rows, 30 non-tutorial trials: 5 butterflies x 6, clickHit 14/30). Counted 100 participant result files in the repo. GA_Population_Data.csv (42.7 MB) seen in the listing only.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Read via the Research Square preprint (CC BY 4.0), not the paywalled Nature version: the 757 morphotypes from 397 species scanned from the Collins Butterfly Guide, the random-forest results (65-69% variance explained), and the data availability statement pointing to GitHub. The Nature version's added behavioural experiment is described only in the abstract; I inferred its design from the repo files.

a1_downloadable.note: Checked: public GitHub repo, no login; CSVs downloaded and parsed with pandas.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked: motion-confusion inputs (left/right/up/down EMD energy) are columns in DF_EMD.csv; confusion is a one-line Michelson contrast of them. In the human game, clickHit (hit or miss) is a column.

a3_inputs_present.note: Checked: 790 wing PNGs plus pattern-statistic table are in the repo; no identifier lookups needed.

a4_units_stated.note: EMD energies are unitless model outputs; pattern statistics are undocumented in the repo but on a consistent scale. Not a blocker given the other failures.

a5_enough_rows.note: Checked: the unit for 'wing pattern -> motion confusion' is the morphotype, 790 rows (paper says 757), under the ~1,500 regression bar. The measured human-game label has ~3,000 trials (100 files x 30, extrapolated from P001) but only 5 butterfly morphotypes, so for pattern effects n = 5.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <5 MB for the morphotype tables; 42.7 MB for GA populations
a6_fits_laptop.note: Checked file sizes in the repo listing.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Checked: 790 morphotypes and 413 species names in the files versus 757 and 397 in the preprint; likely the guide's extra entries or name variants. Tolerable discrepancy, but unresolved.

a8_label_provenance.note: Checked: the motion-confusion label is the output of the authors' deterministic EMD vision model run on Blender renders of the same wing images that would be the features. A learned model would only emulate this simulator (a surrogate), not learn biology; the GA fitness is the same EMD output.

existing_models.name: The paper's own random forests on hand-crafted wing-pattern statistics
existing_models.score_and_split: 65-69% variance explained for forwards and sideways confusion, 90% for forwards energy (out-of-bag, random over morphotypes; from preprint text). R code in the repo.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Behavioural validation with real avian predators; the Nature version adds a human game but with only 5 butterflies.

backbone.name: None appropriate; a generic image model (e.g. DINOv2) could embed wing PNGs, but the target is a simulator output

integration.partner_dataset: Wiemers et al. 2020 European butterfly phylogeny (already used by the authors)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: None beyond the paper's own phylogenetic analysis; there is no measured predation outcome across many species to join to.

controls.positive_control: Recover the paper's finding that forewing contrast drives forwards confusion.
controls.external_validation: None; no independent measured predation-by-pattern dataset.

honest_claim_h3: A model could only claim to approximate the authors' EMD simulator's output for 790 guide-illustration wing patterns, not predict real predator capture.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a butterfly's wing-pattern image to predict how much its flapping flight misleads a predator's motion vision.
plain_idea.train_on: Scanned dorsal wing illustrations from a field guide, 790 morphotypes (species-by-sex) from about 400 European species, with pattern statistics.
plain_idea.predict: Motion-confusion scores, which come from the authors' computer model of bird motion vision run on simulated 3D flight, not from any measurement of predators.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would give a fast proxy for a slow render-plus-simulation pipeline, but that proxy teaches nothing new about biology and the simulator is already free to run.

ml_idea: Considered: regress EMD motion confusion from wing images or pattern statistics across 790 morphotypes with a phylogeny-blocked split; or predict human hit/miss from butterfly and flight path in the catch game. Both fail: the first label is simulator output on too few rows, the second has only 5 butterflies.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from file sizes seen in the repo listing; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Already done: the confusion label is EMD model output (A8) and there are 790 morphotypes (A5).

verdict_reason: Data are clean and public on GitHub, but the cross-species label (motion confusion) is the output of the authors' own vision simulator computed from the wing images (A8), covering only 790 morphotypes (A5). The one measured label, human hit/miss in a catch game (~3,000 trials), covers just 5 butterflies.
